outcome_exposure.purpose: Quantify whether the failed mean-nest-success replication can plausibly be attributed mainly to low design sensitivity or small monitored-nest samples, and decompose mean nest production into success frequency versus brood size among successful nests.

common_panel.definition: Exact Humble same-panel diagnostic intersection: REPRO lag-1 rows with the previously frozen colony-wide chick state available under the V2 season-key rules.
common_panel.controls: Same prior-size z score and colony fixed effects used in the existing same-panel diagnostic.

detectability_simulation.benchmark_effect: Use beta_ref = 0.10402777305744605, the already observed colony-wide chick-state coefficient on the exact common panel. This is a benchmark, not a hypothesized REPRO effect.
detectability_simulation.noise: Estimate residual SD from the common-panel REPRO mean-state model after prior-size and colony fixed effects; simulate Gaussian residual noise in the control-residualized subspace.
detectability_simulation.predictor: Observed standardized REPRO mean chicks-to-creche-per-monitored-nest state.
detectability_simulation.test: For each simulated dataset, refit the same coefficient and evaluate it against 9,999 within-predictor-season REPRO-state permutations using the existing one-sided upper-tail rule.
detectability_simulation.interpretation: This is conditional design sensitivity if the REPRO state truly carried a coefficient of the stated standardized magnitude. It does not account for all latent-variable measurement mismatch.

sampling_stability.rule: Within each common-panel colony-season, resample monitored nests with replacement at the observed sample size; recompute mean chicks per nest and within-season z-standardization.
sampling_stability.statistic: Pearson correlation between each bootstrap REPRO state vector and the original REPRO state vector across the 61 common-panel rows.
sampling_stability.name: bootstrap state stability
sampling_stability.boundary: Do not call this a formal test-retest reliability coefficient.

production_decomposition.identity: mean chicks reaching creche per monitored nest = proportion of monitored nests with at least one creched chick × mean creched chicks among successful monitored nests.
production_decomposition.success_frequency: Use the already prespecified binary-any-creche sensitivity only in its original non-rescue role.

conditional_brood_size.definition: Among monitored nests with >=1 creched chick, mean creched chicks per successful nest.
conditional_brood_size.standardization: Within island-season z score among colony-seasons where the metric is defined; require at least 3 finite colonies in the season.
conditional_brood_size.model: Same next-year relative-growth response, prior-size control and colony fixed effects.
conditional_brood_size.inference: 100,000 within-predictor-season label permutations; post hoc descriptive only.

decision_language.if_benchmark_power_high_and_bootstrap_st: State that limited panel size alone is unlikely to explain the non-replication, while measurement error and sampling selectivity remain possible.
decision_language.if_benchmark_power_low: State that under-detection remains a substantial explanation and do not interpret metric mismatch biologically.
decision_language.decomposition: Use the decomposition only to describe which component of monitored-nest production carries any directional signal; it cannot rescue the failed frozen primary endpoint.

claim_boundaries: Do not convert any diagnostic p-value into a new primary or confirmatory result.
Do not use a significant success-frequency sensitivity to rescue the failed REPRO primary endpoint.
Do not claim that penguins perceive creche counts, chick visibility or public information from this diagnostic.
Do not claim that monitored-nest sampling noise is absent even if design detectability is high.
Do not modify the JBI paper-level conclusion that the colony-wide late-season state is not interchangeable with generic nest productivity.
